title: The internal-Hom comparison for a bounded free model
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell
e p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and an integer $n\geq1$. Put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $T$ be a scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible. On the small etale site $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ take the constant coefficient ring sheaf $A_{T,\mathrm{et}}$ and its module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Let $P'$ be a bounded cochain complex whose terms are finite free $A_{T,\mathrm{et}}$-modules, meaning isomorphic to finite direct sums of $A_{T,\mathrm{et}}$, and let $N$ be a bounded cochain complex of $A_{T,\mathrm{et}}$-modules with constructible cohomology [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes].

Let $
u_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}	o T_{\mathrm{et}}$ be the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], with the constant coefficient identification and exact module pullback $
u_T^*$ of [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact]. Use derived internal Hom on each of these ringed sites [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. The canonical evaluation comparison
$$

u_T^*R\mathcal Hom_A(P',N)\longrightarrow R\mathcal Hom_A(
u_T^*P',
u_T^*N)
$$
is an isomorphism. Here the comparison is the one induced by pulling back evaluation: under the canonical bounded finite-free Hom-complex models [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-bounded-free-rhom-model], it is induced by the termwise maps $
u_T^*\mathcal Hom_A(P'^i,N^j)	o\mathcal Hom_A(
u_T^*P'^i,
u_T^*N^j)$ obtained by currying the pullback of $\mathcal Hom_A(P'^i,N^j)\otimes_A P'^i	o N^j$ [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor]. The second variable requires no etale finite-Tor hypothesis. Use the size convention of [def-weil-size-convention], so that the two coefficient sites are small in the universe used for module sheaves.

proof.text: The module tensor unit is dualizable. The strong monoidal constant-sheaf functor preserves its dual, so the constant coefficient sheaf is dualizable. Induct on the rank to prove its finite coproducts dualizable, identifying each successor coproduct with a binary biproduct, using the binary-biproduct lemma and the zero-object case. Transport duals across the given basis isomorphisms to obtain dualizability of every term of P. These are proved generic results in WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Dualizable and Sites.ConstantSheafMonoidal, with the finite-coproduct induction supplied privately in this module.

Convert the supplied support bounds to IsStrictlyGE and IsStrictlyLE. Apply the proved DerivedCategory.isDualizable_Q_obj to P: a bounded complex with dualizable terms is dualizable in the derived category. This implements the current blueprint finite dual-complex and signed totalization computation using the existing proved library theorem, without a second Hom-complex model.

The comparison inverse image is an exact flat-preserving strong monoidal left adjoint by the existing comparison-site instances. Apply Functor.residueDerivedMonoidal and transport along leftDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory. Its oplax tensorator is exactly the four-factor canonical tensor comparison of def-sf-evaluation-hom-site-comparison: siteComparisonTensorIso_hom_app exposes this tensorator, and siteComparisonDerivedMonoidal_δ proves its canonical three-factor expression. Expanding the final tensor of two maps gives exactly the original four factors. The strong structure is selected only after a proved existence theorem has prescribed all these components; the monoidality proof import remains private.

For a dualizable K choose its right dual and use the braiding to obtain the left exact pairing. The proved Functor.Monoidal.isIso_ihomComparison_app_of_exactPairing makes the canonical internal-Hom comparison invertible for every second argument. The definition siteComparisonEvaluationHom is this canonical comparison. The equation siteComparisonEvaluationHom_eq_curry, proved by ihomComparison_app_eq_curry and the component formula for the inverse tensorator, verifies its original evaluation specification: curry the inverse canonical tensor comparison followed by pullback of evaluation. Apply this with K=Q(P), M=Q(N). No boundedness, constructibility, or Tor assumption on M is needed by this stronger generic argument.

proof_origin.place: Bounded finite-free dual and evaluation argument, implemented through the proved generic dualizability and internal-Hom-comparison library theorems; Q3 stage 3.

blueprint_update.statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum, a prime $\ell\ne p$, an integer
$n\geq1$, $A=A_{E,n}$, and let $T$ be a scheme on which $\ell$ is
invertible. Let $P'$ be a bounded complex of finite free
$A_{T,\Et}$-modules, so that $P'$ is
site-perfect in the sense of
[def-weil-site-perfect-complex], and let $N$ be a bounded complex of
$A$-module sheaves with constructible cohomology on the small étale site
of $T$, in the sense of
[def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. For the comparison morphism
$\nu_T:T_{\Proet}\to T_{\Et}$ of
[def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] the comparison map of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom],

$$
\nu_T^*R\mathcal H om_A(P',N)\longrightarrow
R\mathcal H om_A(\nu_T^*P',\nu_T^*N),
$$

is an isomorphism.

proof.text:
Write $P'^\vee=R\mathcal H om_A(P',A_T)$, so that
$P'^{\vee,i}=\mathcal H om_A(P'^i,A_T)$ is again finite free. For a
bounded complex $P'$ of finite free modules the termwise identity
$\mathcal H om_A(P'^i,N^j)\cong(P'^i)^\vee\otimes_AN^j$ of
[lem-sf-hom-finite-projective], with the total-complex signs, is a
computation of finite free modules and uses nothing about $N$ beyond its
being a complex of modules; it gives

$$
P'^\vee\otimes_A^LN\cong R\mathcal H om_A(P',N),
$$

the finite free modules being flat, so that the derived tensor product of
[def-weil-derived-tensor] is computed by the ordinary tensor complex.
The comparison pullback $\nu_T^*$ is exact, is monoidal and carries finite
free modules to finite free modules by
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]; hence
$\nu_T^*(P'^\vee)\cong(\nu_T^*P')^\vee$ termwise, and the same computation
on the pro-étale side, applied to the bounded complex $\nu_T^*P'$ of
finite free modules and to $\nu_T^*N$, gives

$$
R\mathcal H om_A(\nu_T^*P',\nu_T^*N)
\cong(\nu_T^*P')^\vee\otimes_A^L\nu_T^*N
\cong\nu_T^*\bigl(P'^\vee\otimes_A^LN\bigr)
\cong\nu_T^*R\mathcal H om_A(P',N).
$$

Both the comparison map and this composite are induced by the evaluation of
[lem-sf-hom-finite-projective] and its pullback, so they agree, and the
comparison is an isomorphism.
